newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-RAVANELLI LONGS FOR JUVENTUS GLORY DAYS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RAVANELLI LONGS FOR JUVENTUS GLORY DAYS.

text.p: Italy striker Fabrizio Ravanelli says he still cannot understand why Juventus sold him to Middlesbrough after winning the European Cup last season and that he dreams of returning to serie A.

He also said in an interview with the Rome daily newspaper La Repubblica on Friday that he sympathised with former Juventus team mate Gianluca Vialli, who has been unable to get back into Chelsea's first team line-up recently.

"I have no answer," the prolific striker said when asked why the Italian league leaders had sold him, adding that it had been a hurried decision and he had nobody to tell him to think it over carefully before deciding.

"Time and distance don't help. I hoped to understand it but instead it's still a mystery to me. Maybe it was an economic decision for everybody but billions don't make you win and Fabrizio Ravanelli needs to win," he said.
Ravanelli, whose premier league club are now bottom of the table in England, said returning to Juventus would be a dream come true but it was not going to happen in a hurry.
"I'm not escaping from Middlesbrough, I am not a traitor, I want to leave my club in the premier league, where I found it. In June, well, it will be different.
"Fabrizio Ravanelli has stayed a 'Juventino' and will always be," he said.

Middlesbrough have had a wretched run in the league, winning only four of their 22 games this season, despite spending lavishly in recent years on foreign imports such as Emerson and Juninho of Brazil and Ravanelli.

The Italian, who signed a four-year contract with Middlesbrough, said he had spoken to former Juventus captain Vialli and they could hardly believe what had happened to two of the key players who helped Juventus to win the European Cup.
Vialli told an Italian television station on Wednesday that he was not willing to put up with his situation for much longer. "It's not a very happy time for me," he said.

Ravanelli said: "He is worse off than me. He told me about his knee, about (coach Ruud) Gullit who never plays him. Incredible. If I close my eyes, I see myself with Luca at the Olympic Stadium while we are kissing the cup. And now we are here."
"The England that I was expecting was not a last place. Even a child could understand that," he said.

Middlesbrough were also docked three points on Tuesday for failing to play a match against Blackburn on December 21 after manager Bryan Robson reported that 23 of his players were either ill with influenza or injured.
Ravanelli caused a flurry the same day when he said he thought his club were doomed to relegation.
He told La Repubblica that the words had been put into his mouth and said he and his family enjoyed living in England where he had discovered the delights of playing darts in the pub.
However, asked whether he wanted to have more children, he replied: "Yes, but we'll do it in Italy."
